title: Berlin hotel cap

turns.user: What's the hotel nightly cap for Berlin?

spans.text: City-specific hotel cap. That lives in the expense limits policy. Searching.

hits.heading: Daily meal limits by band
hits.text:
Daily meal limits by band

| Band | Daily meal limit |
| --- | --- |
| Band 1 | EUR 45 |
| Band 2 | EUR 60 |
| Band 3 | EUR 70 |
| Band 4 and above | EUR 90 |

The daily meal limit is a cap on actual spend where per diem is not claimed. An
employee may claim per diem or actual meal costs, not both.

hits.heading: Exceeding a limit
hits.text:
Exceeding a limit

Where a cost exceeds the applicable limit, the employee may claim up to the limit
and must absorb the remainder personally, unless a prior written exception was
granted by the budget holder.

spans.text: I have the limits documents here. Berlin is a standard European city cap, so EUR 200 a night.

The hotel nightly cap for Berlin is **EUR 200 per night**.

That figure is inclusive of local tourist tax, and exclusive of breakfast where breakfast is billed separately.

If you go over the cap you can claim up to EUR 200 and would need to cover the difference yourself, unless your budget holder has granted a written exception in advance.

Source: expense-05-limits-updated, "Hotel nightly caps".
